O.outcome_detail: alignment of perceived factors affecting minoritized students’ participation in computing

cells.quote: First, teacher and administrator perceptions about what may impact minoritized students’ participation in computing programs were not always in alignment with what the students, themselves, identified.
cells.note: The study reports a qualitative mismatch, not a quantitative effect. The interview and survey setting and duration are not stated in the provided study text.

O.outcome_detail: relationship between elementary and high-school grades

cells.quote:
The main purpose of the study, which is here summarized, has been to make a similiar investigation of the relationship between elementary and high-school training.
Only such records were included in this study as showed the completion of at least the last four years of the elementary school and the first two years of the high school. There were 106 records available from the Iowa city schools under this arbitrary standard.
cells.note: The supplied study text is truncated before reporting the correlation or any direction/effect.

O.outcome_detail: suitability for dealing with cold start in user-adaptive systems

cells.quote: It was trialled in the domain of learning Linux concepts. This showed that the interactive open learner modelling approach was suitable for dealing with cold start in user-adaptive systems.
cells.note: The study text reports a trial and a suitability finding but does not state a comparison condition, sample details, study design, or quantitative effect.

D.comparison: initial learner model before the dialogue

O.outcome_detail: learner-model coverage and approval of beliefs

cells.quote: The study showed that, compared to the initial learner models (before the learners engaged in interactive open leaner modelling dialogue), the resultant learner models included more beliefs about the learner, and most of these beliefs were approved by both the learners and the teacher.
cells.note: The study reports more learner-model beliefs and approval by learners and a teacher, but no printed effect size.

cells.quote: The study showed that STyLE-OLM would be beneficial both for more knowledgeable and less knowledgeable learners - the former were engaged in reflective interactions about the domain, while the later were provoked to inspect their models and challenge the robustness of these models.
cells.note: The study reports different forms of reflection across learner-knowledge groups rather than a single better-versus-worse effect; no effect size is printed.
